answer: Agents maintaining networks across a harbor jetty, a highland meadow, and a desert oasis resist Sybil attacks using graph-theoretic trust routing. Nodes exchange capacity-bounded bilateral credit edges based on mutual interaction history. An adversary incurs the scarce cost of obtaining authentic trust links from honest peers, as synthetic identities cannot expand the bottleneck cut capacity. However, this model severely throttles transaction throughput for legitimate newcomer agents.
